A1.justification: Both PDFs describe COGNOS. All 17 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v2, including appendices, support comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures. Localized layout defects in v2 do not prevent substantive comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments across four datasets and twelve backbones, including component ablations, sensitivity analyses, and comparisons with Floss.

after.justification: V2 reports original seven-dataset comparisons, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, residual diagnostics, and computational timing measurements.

M1.justification: V1's raw-residual MMD, lag-autocorrelation penalty, and automatic loss weighting are replaced by activity masking, spectral whitening, standardized Haar-wavelet MMD, and gradient balancing. The forward Kalman/backward RTS pipeline becomes an offline-calibrated ARKS filter with adaptive modes, a chi-squared circuit breaker, and buffered window aggregation (v2 Section 4 and Algorithm 1).

E1.justification: V2 retains MSL, SMAP, SWaT, and PSM and actually evaluates three additional datasets: GECCO water-quality monitoring, SWAN space-weather data, and the heterogeneous univariate UCR anomaly archive. These substantially broaden the represented data and application domains.

E2.justification: The backbone comparison retains Autoformer, DLinear, MICN, and TimesNet, removes eight other v1 backbones, and adds CrossAD, KAN-AD, LSTM-AE, ModernTCN, and TimeMixer++. V1's evaluated Floss comparison disappears. V2 Table 9 also adds moving-average and low-pass controls applied to MSE-trained models.

E3.justification: V2 adds four range-AUC/VUS metrics for three backbones on five datasets, retaining affiliation F1 and point-adjusted F1, now labeled Std-F1. Reported settings also change: SMAP dimensionality goes from 25 to 1, MSL training size from 44,653 to 46,653, and window lengths and model configurations are revised in Table 6. These are reported setting changes, not merely additional disclosure.

E4.justification: V1's twelve-backbone ablations on MSL/PSM become KAN-AD ablations across five datasets, with additional MSE-plus-filter controls. The lambda sensitivity study becomes a circuit-breaker confidence study on SMAP/SWAN. V2 also replaces diagnostic case studies and adds computational-efficiency analysis.

E5.justification: The reported fixed random seed changes from 2021 in v1's Detailed Experiments to 2025 in v2 Appendix D. Both retain 95% white-noise confidence bands for autocorrelation diagnostics; neither reports repeated-run performance uncertainty.

E6.justification: Performance and ablation results are extensively replaced, with additional dataset, metric, and timing entries. For example, COGNOS TimesNet/MSL affiliation F1 changes from 0.942 in v1 Table 11 to 0.9171 in v2 Table 2. Changed algorithms and settings prevent interpreting this as a same-setting regression. V1's detailed precision/recall and Floss results are removed.

T1.justification: V2 introduces a decomposition-based problem formulation and Appendix A containing formal propositions and derivations connecting MSE to likelihood, discussing Gaussian MMSE optimality, and analyzing circuit-breaker trigger and recovery dynamics. These substantially extend v1's standard state-space, filtering, and RTS equations.

C1.justification: The universal residual-regularization claim remains, but hypothesis-driven switching and zero-lag anomaly tracking become central contributions in v2. Its introduction adds an explicit Wold-decomposition requirement. The abstract removes v1's quantified 57.9% uplift across twelve backbones and describes a robust adaptive estimator, although optimality claims remain elsewhere.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations concerning frozen sensors, heteroscedasticity, residual trend leakage, and smoothing versus abrupt-anomaly sensitivity. Sections 5.2 and A.3 introduce an onset-focused interpretation and adaptation to persistent shifts, alongside retained discussion of sustained scores. V2 also interprets differing metric gains and claims greater calibration robustness for multivariate data.

D1.justification: V2 adds streaming pseudocode, buffered aggregation and calibration documentation, expands backbone configurations, and discusses memory-driven batch adjustments. Appendix D changes the documented software from PyTorch 2.3.0/CUDA 12.1 to PyTorch 2.1.0/CUDA 11.8. These materially revise reproducibility information, although numerical settings for some new constants and the buffer remain unspecified.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially rewritten around architectural evolution, representation versus reconstruction, and statistical signal processing. V2 adds wavelet, MMD, normalization, and newer-backbone references, removes the Floss/SVD-AE discussion, and newly positions decoupled filtering against potentially degenerate jointly trained Kalman hybrids.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, methodology, and experimental narrative undergo extensive rewriting. V2 adds a dedicated Problem Formulation section and reorganizes the appendix into sections A–D. The author block also changes and contains placeholder affiliation and correspondence text.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the framework diagram, replaces many line-score visualizations with channel heatmaps, restructures performance and ablation tables, and adds timing tables and a new sensitivity display. V1's radar plots disappear. Appendix layout changes substantially, and Figure 3/Table 4 captions visibly overlap on v2 page 8.

improvement.justification: V2's broader datasets, threshold-independent metrics, and implementation and timing details improve scrutiny. However, it removes Floss and broad cross-backbone ablations while substantially changing the algorithm. It also contains unresolved numerical conflicts: KAN-AD/GECCO vanilla affiliation F1 is 0.3278 in Table 2 but 0.3785 in Table 8. Appendix A.2 does not establish that its linear-Gaussian optimality argument applies to the observation-dependent circuit breaker. These benefits and validation problems leave the net quality effect uncertain.
